idiom_name: to_json/from_json free functions plus an explicit to_message converter
implementation_notes: The wire half is library-owned: the message is a dedicated struct, and to_json(nlohmann::json&, const OrderMessage&) / from_json(const nlohmann::json&, OrderMessage&) declared in its namespace are found by argument-dependent lookup, so `nlohmann::json j = msg;` and `msg = j.get<OrderMessage>()` route through them without touching private members. The domain half stays explicit: an OrderMessage to_message(const Order&) free function in one translation unit flattens the aggregate. Neither the entity nor the message type knows the other, and the encoder never sees the domain object.
pitfalls: from_json must decide what a missing key means: at() throws (fail loud) while value() defaults silently, and mixing the two across fields is how absent values become plausible wrong data.
ADL hooks need the message type's complete definition in scope; splitting declaration and definition across translation units produces template-instantiation errors that read like mapper bugs.
A free-function mapper cannot receive collaborators: promote it to a small mapper class as soon as the mapping needs configuration or a resolver.

variants.name: protoc-generated message classes (schema-first)
variants.idiom_name: generated google::protobuf::Message classes plus a hand-written domain conversion
variants.implementation_notes: When the message contract is IDL-owned, protoc generates the message class, its accessors and the wire parser, so the mapper shrinks to a small conversion function assigning fields between Order and proto::OrderMessage - the structural half is still yours, and the schema's compatibility rules (field numbers, reserved ranges) replace hand-written version handling. Choose it when several services share the schema or a schema registry already governs the channel.
pitfalls: Generated message classes are mutable builders: returning one from the mapper passes a value that callers can still mutate.
proto3 scalar fields have no presence, so an unset string is indistinguishable from an empty one - carry absence with optional fields or a wrapper message, and decide it in the mapper.
Regenerating code on every build couples the mapper to the IDL toolchain; keep generated headers out of the domain's include graph.
